about: The screen groups of the Journey Hub, in the order a person meets them. Each group's screens live in its file, in the order shown. See design/hub/README.md for the <screen> format.

groups.title: Login
groups.intro: Sign in with Apple, Google or a one-time code by email. Nobody has a password to remember.

groups.title: Registration
groups.intro: From sign-in to a full Home in about a minute: a profile, a few interests, journeys to follow and a choice about notifications.

groups.title: Feed
groups.intro: Home is chronological and it ends: new chapters from what you follow, then “You're all caught up”.

groups.title: Discover and search
groups.intro: Find journeys by category, place, person or tag. The ranking is simple and easy to explain.

groups.title: Story line
groups.intro: A journey reads as a story: the cover and highlights first, then a timeline in the order things happened, from the first day to the recap.

groups.title: Posts
groups.intro: Posts are entries: photos, clips and words, always part of a journey. Likes and comments stay with the entry.

groups.title: Create
groups.intro: The + button always creates: a new entry first, a new journey second. Both work with no signal.

groups.title: Shared journeys
groups.intro: One person starts a journey and invites friends to add to it. Everyone's entries flow into one story line, and the journey shows on each person's profile.

groups.title: Activity
groups.intro: One calm inbox. New entries are grouped per journey, likes are batched, a digest arrives once a week, and every type can be switched off.

groups.title: Profile
groups.intro: A profile is a shelf of journeys, active and completed. Your own also shows drafts and private journeys, only to you.

groups.title: Settings
groups.intro: Plain controls for notifications, privacy, appearance and your account, including deleting it.

groups.title: Safety
groups.intro: Report and block are always two taps away. Anything flagged is hidden until a person reviews it.

groups.title: States
groups.intro: Slow, offline or broken: every state says what's happening and what you can do next.
